text:
maya: quick heads up — ran the canary perf sweep on prefix caching after the kernel-sched change, results look sketchy :grimacing:

maya: summary: overall cache hit_rate dropped from ~72% -> ~41% on chat-heavy workloads, eviction_rate spiked (~3x), and p95 token latency increased ~18% on the hosted canary cluster (region-us-west2). grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/prefix-cache-canary-1845

devon: whoa that's a big drop. is this specific to chat or also completions/RAG? :eyes:

maya: mostly chat and RAG prompts that have long convo prefixes and structured tool-calls. Completions with short prompts unchanged. Breakdown: chat (avg prefix len 350 tokens) hit_rate 39%, RAG long-doc chains hit_rate 28%, short completion hit_rate 70%

arjun: any clue on root cause? eviction policy? key collisions? kernel change affecting batching warms?

maya: digging in — two likely contributors:
  1) keying: we use sha256(convo_id + roles+prefix_tokens_truncated) — for RAG the prefix_token sequence includes document IDs + chunk offsets. After we switched to the new kernel that coalesces KV segments, we saw more tiny differences in tokenization order for documents (minor whitespace normalization) so keys diverge more. result: more unique keys -> lower reuse.
  2) eviction interplay with batching: the new kernel increases batching coalescing which raises per-worker in-flight prefix cache pressure for short-lived convo variants; combined with LRU global eviction this causes hot prefixes to be evicted before reuse (observed TTL churn).

kyle: are we sure it's not a plain bug in the prefix canonicalization? maybe tokenizer changes in v2?

maya: checked tokenizer diffs — no, tokenization itself stable. it's the metadata we include (doc-offset markers) that changed due to dedupe pass in the RAG preprocessor on the canary. dedupe introduced tiny reorderings for long doc lists. keys now differ even when semantic prefix same.

devon: ugh. so we have two axes: key-stability and eviction policy. got perf numbers for different configs?

maya: yes, quick experiments on canary (same traffic replay):
  - baseline (old kernel + LRU global): hit_rate 71.8% p95 96ms
  - new kernel + LRU global: hit_rate 41.2% p95 114ms
  - new kernel + segmented_lfu (per-convo hotset): hit_rate 59.7% p95 102ms
  - new kernel + key-normalization (strip doc-offsets) + LRU: hit_rate 63.4% p95 100ms
  - new kernel + key-normalization + segmented_lfu: hit_rate 74.1% p95 92ms (best)

maya: so mitigation matrix: stabilize keys (normalize/remove noisy metadata) + change eviction to segmented-LFU per-convo bucket -> best recovery and even slight improvement vs baseline for chat.

arjun: nice. any downsides to segmented_lfu? memory fragmentation? implementation cost?

kyle: segmented LFU needs per-bucket counters; cost ~ +6% RAM in our tests, complexity up front but limits cross-convo thrash. Also need bounded bucket count so we don't blow map overhead.

maya: noted. also need a key-normalization guard so we don't strip legitimate disambiguators (some customers rely on doc-offsets). plan: make normalization configurable per-customer or per-route (RAG routes enable normalization by default).

devon: what about warmup strategies? can we pre-warm hot prefixes for known PLG flows (signup flows, onboarding chat templates)?

maya: yes — two quick warmup ideas we tested:
  - proactive prefix push during canary deploys: take top-1k convo prefixes from prod-telemetry and pre-insert into cache on rollout -> reduces cold-start miss by ~12% for first 10 minutes.
  - sticky routing: route a user's requests to same worker for short window (sticky session) -> reduces cross-worker misses for small fleets. improved hit_rate by ~6% but slightly increases instance imbalance.

arjun: sounds like feature flags are needed. Do we have a rollout plan?

maya: proposed rollout:
  1) revert kernel-sched change on canary while we ship fixes (if we can't fast mitigate) OR keep kernel but disable aggressive coalescing flag (quick revert-safe knob).
  2) ship key-normalization as a config (route-level) behind feature flag: enable_prefix_key_norm_v1.
  3) add segmented_lfu as opt-in eviction policy: prefix_eviction=segmented_lfu.
  4) implement pre-warm job for top-n prefixes and sticky routing as optional opt-in.

kyle: any perf regressions from segmented_lfu path? we saw p95 back to 92ms in canary but need longer soak. also add unit tests for canonical key generator.

maya: agree. tests + integration:
  - unit: key normalization permutations, ensure no semantic collisions for known datasets
  - perf: 24h soak in staging with mixed chat/RAG traffic replay
  - safety: per-customer opt-out if they need raw doc-offset semantics

maya: config snippet i'll push to PR description:

```yaml
prefix_cache:
  key_builder: "sha256(convo_id + normalized_prefix)"
  normalization: { strip_offsets: true, collapse_whitespace: true, sort_doc_ids: true }
  eviction_policy: segmented_lfu
  max_entries_per_bucket: 50000
  global_max_entries: 1000000
  ttl_seconds: 3600
```

devon: nice. timeline? can we have key-norm + segmented_lfu in staging by EOD tomorrow?

maya: aiming to open PR today, run unit tests tonight, perf soak tomorrow. blocker: need arjun to help with segmented_lfu implementation review and kyle to own feature-flag gating.

arjun: on it, will review seg-lfu PR today.

kyle: i'll take flag scaffolding + canary job changes.

sre-bot: deploy-canary report: canary cluster 3/3 nodes drained for newer image; metrics collection enabled.

maya: action items:
  - maya: PR for key-normalization + tests (WIP)
  - arjun: segmented_lfu impl + review
  - kyle: feature flag + canary rollout job changes
  - devon: coordinate staging traffic replay and measurement dashboard

maya: final note — for customers using structured outputs (json/tool calls) we should consider skipping prefix cache for the structured-prompt block since it has high variability (many small changes). that reduced noise in experiments.

devon: ack. thanks maya, let's sync tomorrow 10am. :+1:

maya: thanks everyone!
